thread.title: Google and Facebook spends 2017 more than $18 million and $11.5 million respectively for lobbying

author: Jasmin Chavez
title: Google and Facebook spends 2017 more than $18 million and $11.5 million respectively for lobbying
text:
January 24, 2018 Google and Facebook spends 2017 more than $18 million and $11.5 million respectively for lobbying 
Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL) has spent more than its tech competitors in lobbying in 2017, as Amazon.com Inc, Facebook Inc (NASDAQ:FB) and Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) set company records for current year, federal disclosures revealed. 
The bonanza for telecom and tech lobbying arrived as both sectors undergone tough scrutiny in Washington, and a huge number of industries looked for capitalizing on a tax overhaul and regulatory rollback in President Donald Trump’s initial year in office. 
The disclosures revealed that Facebook has spent over $11.5 million and Google has spent in excess of $18 million in 2017, as legislators scrutinized the both companies over questions involving Russia’s use of their giant platforms in attempt to influence the 2016 election. 
Along with Twitter, both of the companies have approved that millions of their users were exposed to false news reports, ads and deceitful social media posts from Russian operatives. 
All the three companies have sent executives to appear before Congress at the end of October accounted for the Russian activities happened on its platform. They have promised to expand their content screening techniques earlier than the 2018 midterm elections. 
Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOGL) has beaten all other companies during the fourth quarter with spending over $4.6 million, though some trade groups spent considerably more during the period. On the whole, the annual expenditures of search giant indicated a record for the company when subsidiaries are omitted. It also lobbied on a bill that tries to restrain online sex trafficking, and it conflicted the Federal Communications Commission (FCC)’s withdrawing of open internet rules. 
While lobbying in favor of the FCC’s move, Comcast was the second largest spender in the fourth quarter amongst single companies, spending in excess of $4.3 million. AT&T Inc., which also backed FCC’s decision, spent over $3.6 million even it has fought for its planned merger with Time Warner Inc. and battled for Trump’s tax bill. 
During the year, Amazon has spent almost $13 million, involving above $3.3 million in the fourth quarter. The company has tackled some different pressures compared to the platform companies, however, its size has upset some external groups even as it is functional on legislation concerning government procurement, the taxation of goods sold online and regulations of drones for delivery. The President Trump has also panned the company because Jeff Bezos its founder and CEO possesses the Washington Post. 
Tech companies also lobbied highly on taxes and immigration. Apple spent in excess of $7 million during the year. Earlier this month, the company announced that it will bring hundreds of billions of dollars stored abroad currently back to the US, where it would pay almost $38 billion in taxes and spend more on domestic offices and jobs.
